title: Wind Dancer Guide — Stages, Evasion, Hit Consumption and Spirit Value
summary: Wind Dancer is a Spirit gem that reserves 30 Spirit. It is a persistent defensive buff that grants Stages; each Stage gives increased Evasion. When you are Hit by an enemy, you lose Stages. Since the 0.2 change it consumes on any Enemy Hit rather than only Melee Attacks, making it a general defensive layer for evasion builds.
description: Wind Dancer deep guide: how Stages are gained, maximum Stages, Evasion per Stage, what Hit consumes a Stage, the 0.2 Melee-to-Enemy-Hit change, whether a hit consumes all Stages, what happens at zero Stages, Knockback and AoE, DoT and Evade/Block/Deflect behaviour, boss red-flash attacks, fresh-area reset, Weapon Set limits and the 30 Spirit tradeoff with Herald / Combat Frenzy / Ghost Dance.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial
imageAlt: Wind Dancer evasion spirit skill icon

sections.title: Quick Answer
paragraphs: Wind Dancer reserves 30 Spirit and gives you Stages, each Stage adding increased Evasion. It is a persistent defensive layer for evasion-based builds.
When you are Hit by an enemy, you lose Stages. Since the 0.2 change, any Enemy Hit consumes a Stage, not just Melee Attacks, so it helps against ranged and AoE enemies too.

At zero Stages you lose the Evasion bonus but are not penalised otherwise. Entering a new area resets you to zero Stages, so you rebuild them as you fight. The 30 Spirit competes with Herald, Combat Frenzy and Ghost Dance.

properties.label: Spirit
notes: Cheap; often run alongside another small Spirit skill.

properties.label: Effect
notes: Each Stage adds Evasion; consumed by enemy hits.

properties.label: Trigger change
notes: Originally Melee Attack only; now any enemy hit consumes a Stage.

properties.label: Acquisition
notes: Obtained from an Uncut Skill Gem; enabled in the skill panel.

sections.title: Requirements
paragraphs: No special attribute gate. The real requirement is that your build already invests in Evasion — Wind Dancer multiplies Evasion, so on a low-Evasion character the bonus is small.

keyValues.label: Evasion investment
notes: Wind Dancer scales your Evasion; low Evasion = low payoff.

sections.title: Persistent Buff
paragraphs: Wind Dancer is a persistent buff: once enabled it stays on, reserving 30 Spirit, and passively tracks your Stages. You do not activate it per hit; it is always watching.

keyValues.label: State
notes: Reserves 30 Spirit for the whole map or fight.

keyValues.label: Stages
notes: No manual input; Stages change from combat events.

sections.title: Defensive Stages
paragraphs: You gain Stages over time while fighting (and, depending on the patch, from evading enemy hits). The maximum number of Stages is small — commonly four at higher gem levels — and each Stage grants increased Evasion Rating, the percentage scaling with the gem's level.
More Stages means more Evasion, which raises your chance to evade attacks. The bonus is multiplicative on your Evasion, so it is strongest when your base Evasion is already high.

This is a mechanic explanation, not a survival calculator. A higher Evasion number does not guarantee a fixed reduction in damage taken, because actual evasion depends on the attacker's accuracy and other modifiers.
bullets: Stages build during combat; maximum is a small number (commonly 4).
Each Stage adds increased Evasion (scales with gem level).
Bonus multiplies your Evasion; best on already-evasive builds.

sections.title: Hit Consumption
paragraphs: Since the 0.2 change, being Hit by an enemy consumes a Stage. It is no longer limited to Melee Attacks — ranged hits and AoE also consume a Stage. A single hit consumes one Stage, not all of them, so several hits in a row strip Stages gradually.

When you reach zero Stages, the Evasion bonus disappears but nothing else bad happens; you simply lose the layered Evasion until you rebuild Stages. Knockback and AoE still count as enemy hits if they actually strike you.
bullets: Any Enemy Hit consumes one Stage (since 0.2, not just Melee).
One hit = one Stage, not all Stages.
Zero Stages = no bonus, no extra penalty.

sections.title: Evasion Analysis
paragraphs: Damage-over-Time effects (poison, burning, ignored ground) do not consume Stages, because they are not enemy hits. Evade, Block and Deflect also do not consume Stages — those are successful avoids, not hits taken.

Boss red-flash telegraphed attacks are still enemy hits and will consume a Stage when they land. Tooltip Evasion and real evade chance are not the same: actual evasion depends on the attacker's accuracy, so do not read a higher tooltip Evasion as a fixed survival gain.
Low-Evasion gear makes Wind Dancer weak: the percentage bonus is applied to a small base, so the absolute Evasion gained is minor. It is a multiplier, not a flat floor.
bullets: DoT, Evade, Block, Deflect do NOT consume Stages.
Boss red-flash hits DO consume a Stage.
Tooltip Evasion is not real evade chance; gear matters.

sections.title: Spirit Budget
paragraphs: At 30 Spirit, Wind Dancer is cheap. The tradeoff is against Herald of Ice / Herald of Thunder, Combat Frenzy and Ghost Dance — all useful defensive or offensive Spirit skills. Because it is cheap, many evasion builds run it alongside one of those.

keyValues.label: Reservation
notes: Leaves room for another small Spirit skill.

keyValues.label: Vs Herald / Frenzy / Ghost Dance
notes: Pick what your build needs most; Wind Dancer is the evasion layer.

sections.title: Support Compatibility
paragraphs: Wind Dancer is a persistentbuff rather than an attack, so most supports do not apply. The value comes from the gem level (more Evasion per Stage) and from your own Evasion investment, not from socketed supports.

keyValues.label: Gem level
notes: Higher level = more Evasion per Stage.

keyValues.label: Evasion gear
notes: Your Evasion investment decides the absolute payoff.

sections.title: Mapping Value
paragraphs: In maps you are hit frequently by many enemies, which keeps stripping Stages, but you also rebuild them fast between packs. The layered Evasion noticeably cuts incoming hits during clear, especially on evasion builds that already evade well.

steps.label: Fight the pack
steps.action: Engage; Stages build and are consumed by hits.

sections.title: Bossing Value
paragraphs: On bosses, big telegraphed hits consume Stages one at a time; the Evasion bonus helps dodge smaller hits but a single heavy hit still lands and strips a Stage. It is a decent defensive layer but not a substitute for proper avoidance and defences.

steps.label: Survive the pattern
steps.action: Use the Evasion bonus to dodge chips; avoid reds.
steps.result: Stages absorb some chip damage but big hits still land.

sections.title: Build Usage
paragraphs: Ice Shot Deadeye: an evasion bow build that uses Wind Dancer as a standard defensive layer.
Whirling Assault Martial Artist: a dexterity melee build that already stacks Evasion, making the Stages meaningful.
Any evasion-stacking build: if you invest in Evasion, Wind Dancer multiplies it for a cheap 30 Spirit.
bullets: Any build with high Evasion investment.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: No bonus when entering an area: Stages reset to zero on area entry. Direct answer: rebuild Stages by fighting; they return within seconds.
Feels weak: your Evasion is too low. Direct answer: Wind Dancer multiplies Evasion; raise your base Evasion for a real payoff.
Stages vanish in boss fights: red-flash hits consume them. Direct answer: that is expected; dodge the big hits, the bonus helps chips.
Swapped Weapon Set and lost it: you enabled it on only one set. Direct answer: enable Wind Dancer on both sets if you want it always on.

sections.title: Community Evidence
paragraphs: Players widely note the 0.2 change from Melee Attack to Enemy Hit made Wind Dancer far more broadly useful, since ranged and AoE builds now benefit.
The 'entered a new area and lost all Stages' confusion is common; the reset on area entry is intended.
The main debate is 30 Spirit versus Herald / Combat Frenzy / Ghost Dance; evasion builds usually keep Wind Dancer as the defensive pick.
bullets: Recurring note: 0.2 Enemy-Hit change broadened use.
Recurring question: why no Stages in a new area? Reset by design.
Debate: 30 Spirit vs other Spirit skills.
